articles.title: Abergavenny masseuse fits rape alarm after men treat her 'like a sex worker'
articles.summary: Ffion Price, 26, wants better college training after experiencing sexual harassment.
articles.body:
A 26-year-old masseuse says she receives so many inappropriate messages from men that she has started carrying a rape alarm.

Ffion Price, from Gilwern, near Abergavenny, said she even had one physical experience which put her in a "very vulnerable situation", despite years of professional training.

She has fitted a rape alarm in her treatment room and CCTV outside the building, and no longer accepts male clients when she is working alone.

Ffion wants men to understand the harm this behaviour causes, and for colleges and training providers to offer better training on how to deal with such situations.

Following the experience, Ffion posted on Facebook to remind her followers that she is "strictly professional".

She asked men to "think about sending that message before you do", saying they may not realise the impact their behaviour has on therapists and how it can affect the way they feel about their profession.

She is also calling for colleges to introduce a separate safety module covering appropriate massage techniques for male clients, red flags to look out for and what to do if a situation becomes unsafe.

"You don't know who's going to walk through the door, what they're going to be expecting from that treatment and how far they're going to go - and what you would do in that situation if they did take it further, so it's a difficult one.

"I work so hard to get to where I am doing so much training in physiology, anatomy, the human body in general.

"So to be degraded as almost a sex worker is disheartening, it's horrible."

In 2018, Ffion began her training at Coleg Gwent, completing a City & Guilds Level 2 Diploma in Beauty Therapy before progressing to a Level 3 qualification with VTCT Skills.

During her courses, she learnt about tinting, waxing, facials and massage, which was taught as a separate module.

She said she was "briefly" taught not to massage a male client above the knee, but never what to do if a man was aroused or inappropriate.

Ffion said she secured a job at a female-only spa where she worked for five years, completing various additional courses with Clarins Beauty but Ffion said the training was largely catered towards women, with little focus on treating men.

In 2024, Ffion decided to become self-employed, renting a room at a beauty salon and chose to treat both men and women, seeing it as a niche in the town.

"So coming here on my own, I've had to figure out the hard way how to do things differently when a male client comes in," Ffion said.

Since launching her business, Serenity by Ffion, she said she has received inappropriate messages from men almost every other week.

Some, she said, had become "quite clever" in how they approached her, asking whether she could massage "just certain areas".

"I've had people ask for specific massages that I've then had to go and research and be like 'what is this massage', and it'd be extremely inappropriate," she said.

A few months ago, one client made her feel "very awkward" and vulnerable during a massage after failing to use the modesty towel.

Ffion said the man, who was wearing his boxers, became sexually aroused as she was massaging his leg and began grabbing her hand.

After leaving, he showed no embarrassment or remorse and even tried to book another appointment, she said.

Looking back, Ffion said she would have asked him to leave, describing the towel as a "red flag from the start".

"It was the first situation it's happened and to be honest the whole time I felt like I was in the wrong and I was doing something that I shouldn't be doing and that's because of his actions," she said.

Ffion says pornography and the internet had created unrealistic, sexualised expectations of professional massages.

"People are aware that you could go to other countries and have these sorts of treatments and they would be what these men are expecting," she said.

"But it's very different - that's what they offer. But you come over here and it's a professional massage."

Rhianne Evans, 46, from Merthyr Tydfil, has worked in the beauty industry for 25 years.

While she has not had physically bad experiences, she has had to remind male clients of the "protocol", with some pushing their luck with undergarments.

During her time working as a spa manager at the Nant Ddu Lodge in Merthyr Tydfil, she said: "We had some suggestive comments that I suppose could be passed off as a throwaway remark but even so I personally think it's unnecessary.

"It is a very close contact, personal treatment, whether it's a facial or a massage - you are just two of you in a room.

"And I don't think any comments really should be made, you know, suggesting anything otherwise than what they're there for."

After teaching beauty therapy for 20 years in two colleges, Rhianne said safeguarding should be included as a separate model in courses, particularly around dealing with aggressive or suggestive clients.

Rhianne said she used to bring it up as part of a theory session but "I only spoke about it because I experienced it".

She recommended therapists avoiding massaging a male client's stomach during a full-body massage, instead spending more time on areas such as the back, feet and head.

A spokesperson for Gwent College said it was "sorry to hear about the experiences described" and stressed that sexual harassment was "unacceptable".

It explained that while it could not comment on an individual former learner's "precise experience", the courses Ffion did in 2020 and 2021 followed the relevant awarding body's qualification requirements, alongside the professional expertise and wider industry knowledge of its lecturers.

Refering to its current beauty therapy provision, it said it was "delivered by practising beauty therapists and includes training on ethical practice, personal safety and clear professional boundaries when working with clients of all genders".

The spokesperson added the college encouraged learners to "join professional membership bodies for ongoing industry guidance and support".

"We welcome feedback from former learners and regularly review our curriculum and training to ensure they reflect current industry practice and awarding-body requirements," it added.

A spokesperson for VTCT Skills, which sets the core curriculum for the Level 3 Beauty Diploma, said sexual harassment and inappropriate behaviour have "no place" in the workplace, stressing the importance of safe and respectful learning and working environments.

While VTCT Skills said it could not comment on Ffion's training experience, it welcomed wider industry discussion on "challenging" such behaviour and ensuring those who experience harassment are "listened to, supported, and taken seriously".

City & Guilds, who set the core curriculum for the Level 2 Beauty Diploma, declined to comment.

A spokesperson for the Complementary and Natural Healthcare Council (CNHC) said it could not comment on the specific case but stressed that no practitioner should feel "unsafe or harassed, and potentially criminal behaviour should be reported to police.

articles.title: India, Uzbekistan target long-term uranium pact
articles.summary: India News: India and Uzbekistan upgraded their relations to a comprehensive strategic partnership, set an annual trade target of $5 billion and closed in on an a.
articles.body: India and Uzbekistan upgraded their relations to a comprehensive strategic partnership, set an annual trade target of $5 billion and closed in on an agreement for uranium supply to India, as PM Narendra Modi held talks with President Shavkat Mirziyoyev in Tashkent.Modi announced that India would get into a long-term arrangement for supply of uranium from Uzbekistan, a major regional producer and exporter. Both sides agreed to establish a foreign minister-level coordination council to guide all aspects of cooperation under the elevated partnership.Following the talks that focused on expanding cooperation in defence and security, trade and investment, critical minerals, AI, agriculture and health, the two sides signed 11 MoUs. The areas covered included culture, education, mining, Ayurveda, tourism and restoration of Buddhist sites.PM Modi also underscored the need for zero tolerance against terrorism and extremism, saying a stronger India-Uzbekistan partnership will be a powerful force for peace, progress and prosperity in Central Asia.PM Modi and Mirziyoyev endorsed growing defence cooperation between the two countries, including through regular exchanges, capacity-building and joint activities, and expressed in a joint statement their commitment to address common security challenges by further strengthening such cooperation. Going forward, Modi said, both sides will promote direct linkages, co-production and co-development by the defence industries of both nations. “Close defence and security cooperation between our two countries reflects our deep mutual trust,” said the PM.Outlining an ambitious agenda for moving forward with “speed and tangible results” in this new phase of their partnership, the PM said both sides will also work systematically on market access, connectivity, banking and payment systems to achieve the target of $5 billion of trade by 2030.“We will work together to boost win-win cooperation in infrastructure development. Cooperation in DPI, AI, critical minerals, clean energy, space and nuclear energy is making our relationship future-ready,” said Modi, adding that Uzbekistan is at the heart of Central Asia and at the heart of India’s engagement with the region.Both sides believe that while India is one of Uzbekistan’s top 10 trading partners, their annual trade of $1.32 billion remains significantly below its true potential. In the meeting, the two agreed to undertake joint measures to broaden the range of goods traded between the two countries, remove non-tariff barriers and promote industrial cooperation with a view to further increasing bilateral trade turnover. They also decided to create a joint working group to address non-tariff issues and investment barriers.There was also focus on Global South cooperation with PM Modi saying that Uzbekistan’s highest honour for a foreign leader that was conferred on him by the president had left India with the added responsibility of working with Uzbekistan as “Global South partners for the betterment of humanity”.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: US strikes launchers on Iran's Larak Island in first known attack in weeks
articles.summary: Iran says the attack killed some civilians and is the first known US strike on Iran since late July.
articles.body:
US forces have struck two Iranian launchers on Iran's Larak island, a US official said, marking the first known American strikes on Iran since late July.

"Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) forces were observed preparing to launch rockets with sea mines into Strait of Hormuz," the BBC's US partner CBS News quoted US Central Command spokesman Cdr Tim Hawkins as saying.

The IRGC said the attack on Sunday killed and wounded several people, and vowed "response and punishment".

It marks the first known US strike in Iran since US President Donald Trump paused a renewed military campaign in late July. The US said it had finished clearing all mines from the strait's main shipping lane earlier this month.

How the US could try to seize Iran's Kharg Island

US plans to cut off military aid to key Middle East ally, BBC told

Iran says it is 'fully prepared' to counter widened US economic sanctions

Larak Island is just offshore from the key port of Bandar Abbas and sits right on the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway for global shipping.

Iran is currently making tanker traffic pass by this island for checking and reportedly forcing vessels to pay $2m (£1.5m) to cross.

Hossein Mohebbi, the IRGC's spokesman called the attack a "strategic and fatal mistake by the Trump regime" and said that the "enemy will pay the consequences of this miscalculation in both the economic and military fields".

Iran's Tasnim news agency, which is affiliated with the IRGC, said earlier that the attack was carried out by drones. Reports indicate that two people were killed and two others injured, it said.

Trump ​said last week that all mines‌ placed in the Strait of Hormuz by Iran as part of its efforts to blockade the route had been detonated or removed. He said Iran had been warned that any ship ​or boat deploying new mines would be ​destroyed.

Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi described Trump's claim as a "propaganda" deception.

Iran is facing renewed economic pressure after Washington announced a fresh sanctions campaign on 24 August aimed at further isolating Tehran and expanding secondary sanctions against its allies .

Iranian officials and state media have largely dismissed the campaign as a continuation of previous US economic measures, which they argue followed Washington's military failure in the recent conflict.

The US and Israel launched wide-ranging strikes on Iran on 28 February, with Iran responding by attacking Israel, US bases and allied states in the Gulf, and effectively closing the Strait of Hormuz to marine traffic. The Iran war has now crossed its six-month mark.

Some 20% of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas used to travel through before the war began.

articles.title: PM Modi likely to hold bilateral talks with Iranian president
articles.summary: India News: PM Narendra Modi may have a bilateral meeting with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines of the SCO summit in Kyrgyzstan Monday, offici.
articles.body: PM Narendra Modi may have a bilateral meeting with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines of the SCO summit in Kyrgyzstan Monday, official sources said. While Modi landed in Bishkek Sunday, the president was scheduled to arrive Monday morning, according to reports from Tehran.Sources said efforts were on to schedule a meeting between the leaders Monday. This would be the first in-person meeting between Modi and Pezeshkian since the start of the US-Israel war with Iran on Feb 28.The two, in fact, had last met on the margins of the Brics summit in Russia's Kazan in 2024. However, both have spoken with each other on several occasions, including after the West Asia conflict erupted, with Modi stressing the India remains a friend of Iran. Pezeshkian is also likely to visit India for the Brics summit next month.If it happens, the meeting will see Modi reiterate India's position that all issues must be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy. He's also expected to highlight India's focus on ensuring the safety and well being of Indian nationals in the region, along with the importance of unhindered transit of energy and goods. The two will also discuss trade, energy and connectivity ties that have come under strain because of the expiry of US sanctions waiver for the Chabahar port.In a difficult balancing act, India has continued to maintain high-level engagement with Iran while repeatedly expressing solidarity with GCC States that came under attack from Tehran for hosting US bases. However, Tehran also expects India to call out the US and Israel for their Feb 28 strikes at the Brics forum, which is currently helmed by India. With the UAE also in the group, the challenge for India would be to forge a consensus on the West Asia situation that would allow a Brics declaration to be issued.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: More than 20 may be missing after ‘significant flash flood' at Grand Canyon
articles.summary: National Park officials closed down the Bright Angel Canyon area as they anticipated a chance of renewed flash flooding through Monday.
articles.body:
More than 20 people may be missing or unaccounted for after a flash flood ripped through Grand Canyon National Park's Bright Angel Canyon on Saturday.

Strong thunderstorms dropped more than an inch of rain in an hour atop recently burned areas around 2:30 p.m. Saturday, sending a slurry of mud and debris rushing through the canyon. Floodwaters rose more than 5 feet in 10 minutes and destroyed bridges across Bright Angel Creek and forced the closure of one of the park's most difficult trails.

A flash flood watch remained in effect in the Grand Canyon through Monday as forecasters warned of dangerous downpours in Arizona and Utah.

The National Park Service on Sunday morning said 62 campers and hikers were airlifted out of the area. An update released Sunday afternoon indicated more than 20 people could be missing or unaccounted for:

"Grand Canyon National Park staff, in coordination with the Arizona Department of Public Safety, are continuing evacuation and response efforts and working to account for individuals who may have been in the affected area.

"The National Park Service is asking anyone who knows of hikers or backpackers who were in the inner canyon along the Bright Angel Creek corridor on August 29, as well as anyone who had a campground reservation in the affected corridor, to provide information to the National Park Service Investigative Services Branch (ISB).

"This includes individuals who may have been traveling along the North Kaibab Trail from the North Kaibab Trailhead to Phantom Ranch, staying at Bright Angel Campground, or traveling or staying in the area known as 'the Box' north of Phantom Ranch.

"If you know of anyone who may have been hiking or backpacking in these areas, please contact the NPS Investigative Services Branch Tip Line: 888-653-0009," the park service said.

Park officials closed Phantom Ranch, Bright Angel campground, the Phantom Ranch canteen and cabins along with the North Kaibab Trail. The Colorado River was shut down to traffic after metal structures and other debris entered the waterway. The Black Bridge and Silver Bridge crossing the Colorado River was also closed.

Staff warned they may need to make additional inner canyon closures as the chance of additional thunderstorms and heavy rainfall Sunday and Monday threatened to unleash more flash flooding, park officials said.

Cell phone service throughout much of Northern Arizona is difficult to maintain, the park service warned.

"It is nearly impossible to get and keep a signal at Grand Canyon, Marble Canyon, Arizona Strip, and area tribal lands," it said. "Satellite phones are being tested with some success in places outside of the narrowest portions of the canyon."

The Colorado River rose 8 feet in one hour as floodwaters rushed by, according to a U.S. Geological Survey gauge. Waters on Bright Angel Creek increased by more than 5 feet in 10 minutes before the sensor was damaged by flooding.

Saturday's flood occurred a year after the Dragon Bravo Fire ripped through the Grand Canyon's North Rim and destroyed a historic lodge .

Bursts of heavy rain on recently burned landscapes can trigger debris flows, a slurry mix of mud, trees and rocks. A moderate to high-severity fire can alter the physical and chemical makeup of the soil and may make it completely repellent to water.

A park service assessment of the Dragon Bravo burn scar last summer found that "debris flow risk is localized to steep, confined drainages, like Dragon Creek and upper Bright Angel Creek."

Short-duration rain bursts, such as thunderstorm downpours, are more likely to trigger debris flows than long-duration moderate rainfall.

A weather station along Bright Angel Creek measured 1.17 inches of rain between 2 and 3 p.m. Saturday, which far exceeded the National Weather Service's flash flood guidance for the Grand Canyon. That prompted the agency to issue a flash flood warning.

A slight (level 2 of 4) risk of flash flooding remained across Arizona on Sunday and Monday. A flood watch - indicating favorable conditions for flooding - was in effect for a majority of the state through Monday. A flash flood warning - indicating an imminent or occurring flood - was issued just before noon along the Colorado River in northern Arizona, upstream of Grand Canyon National Park.

The weather service said overall coverage of downpours Sunday "should be a bit less" than Saturday, but flooding was more likely in areas that are hit by heavy rainfall multiple hours or days in a row due to "saturated grounds."

A moderate (level 3 of 4) risk of flash flooding was warned in south-central Utah on Monday. That included many recently burned areas in the state, which experienced an extreme burst of fire activity in June.

articles.title: Tectone claims he faced ‘death threats’ after Ironmouse age remarks, as controversial daughter claims ignite online backlash
articles.summary: US Streamers News: Rumble streamer John “Tectone” has claimed that he received death threats after commenting on VTuber Ironmouse’s alleged age and family life. The cont.
articles.body: Rumble streamer John “Tectone” has claimed that he received death threats after commenting on VTuber Ironmouse’s alleged age and family life. The controversy began during his August 27, 2026, livestream, when he watched an old clip that he said showed Ironmouse talking about having a 10-year-old daughter in 2017. Tectone then used that information to claim that Ironmouse could now be around 40 and have a 19-year-old daughter. Those claims about her age have not been independently confirmed. A day later, Tectone said he had received more death threats than ever before.Tectone reacts to Ironmouse clip and claims death threatsDuring the August 27 livestream, Tectone appeared surprised while discussing the old clip. He said that if the person in the clip was Ironmouse, the timeline would mean she had a 19-year-old daughter in 2026.Tectone said:“In 2017, she confirmed that she had a daughter that was 10 years old. That was her?! Wait, so that means Ironmouse has a 19-year-old daughter, and she is actually 40 years old? What the ****?!”He then said the discovery left him shocked and claimed Ironmouse was “pushing 40.”The discussion spread online, with social media users debating the old clip and what it actually showed. However, the available reporting does not independently establish Ironmouse’s age or confirm the details Tectone suggested.The following day, Tectone addressed the reaction to his comments. He claimed that anonymous users had sent him messages threatening his life.He said:“I've never gotten more death threats in my entire life than when a random anonymous user submitted a video to my daily scramble, something that I check every single day, and I reacted to a clip of Ironmouse, and now everybody wants to kill me.”Tectone added that he had received more direct messages about people wanting him dead than at any other point in his life.There is no independent confirmation in the available reports that the alleged threats came specifically from Ironmouse fans. The claim comes from Tectone himself.Tectone says Ironmouse fans “need help”Tectone also criticized people he believed were attacking him over the incident. He said he thought some of Ironmouse’s fans “need help” and said he would continue streaming despite the backlash.He added:“I would say, quite frankly, I think you need help. I do. I do. But that's okay. I will continue being on stream, doing my thing, while your streamer larps as something they're not.”Tectone ended the discussion by saying he did not hate Ironmouse and that he had only commented because the clip appeared during his stream.Ironmouse has not publicly responded to Tectone’s latest comments about her alleged age or the claims surrounding the old video, according to the available reporting.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Grand Canyon flash flooding sparks search for missing hikers
articles.summary: "It was a beautiful day - and then people were screaming," one hiker who was airlifted to safety tells the BBC.
articles.body:
More than 20 people are thought to be missing or unaccounted for after flash flooding swept through parts of the Grand Canyon.

It hit at around 14:30 local time (22:30 BST) on Saturday in Bright Angel Canyon and Phantom Ranch area, according to the National Park Service (NPS).

Sixty-two people have so far been airlifted out of the area, with more expected to follow. No injuries have been reported.

"The whole thing was terrifying," said Nikki Baggs, 41, who was among those to be airlifted out of the bottom of the Grand Canyon on Saturday alongside her two friends.

"It was a beautiful day and then people were screaming, running," she told the BBC.

Baggs said she and her friends had just dropped off their belongings at a cabin in Phantom Ranch - a remote lodge at the bottom of the Grand Canyon - when they decided to venture out to enjoy the nice day. Before they knew it, a flood of water was sweeping through the area.

As soon as the rain hit, Baggs and her friends headed toward higher ground, where they sat at a picnic table, before rangers yelled to them to run again to a different ledge, where they waited with others for hours before they were evacuated at around 21:30 local time.

Baggs said she and her two friends had been looking forward to a steak dinner at Phantom Ranch - but were now just grateful to be alive thanks to a swift response from park rangers.

"It was a really uniquely coordinated effort," she said. "That's what made us feel safe about all of it in an unsafe situation."

The NPS said flooding had caused significant damage in some areas and that trails in the area have been closed. Baggs said she and her friends watched from higher ground as bridges were swept away.

It asked anyone who knew of hikers or backpackers who were in the inner canyon along the Bright Angel Creek corridor on Saturday to get in touch.

The NPS also warned that more thunderstorms and heavy rainfall were forecast for Sunday and Monday, which could lead to "additional flash flooding, debris flows, rockfall and changing trail and river conditions".

The Grand Canyon is one of the most popular national parks in the US, with about five million people visiting each year. The Bright Angel trail is its most popular hike.

articles.title: NEET-PG 2026 smooth; retest for 2.4k Jaipur kids hit by glitch
articles.summary: India News: NEET-PG 2026 was conducted across the country on Sunday for nearly 2.7 lakh candidates appearing at 1,111 centres in 339 cities. A retest will be held.
articles.body: NEET-PG 2026 was conducted across the country on Sunday for nearly 2.7 lakh candidates appearing at 1,111 centres in 339 cities. A retest will be held on Sept 5 for 2,445 candidates at two centres in Jaipur as a glitch disrupted the examination.Dr Abhijat Sheth, president of National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences, said there were no complaints of paper leak, or hacking, and that the examination was conducted in a fair and transparent manner with support from state govts, police, NBEMS experts and faculty members.3-member committee to probe power failure The NEET-PG 2026 examination was conducted across all 36 states and UTs.The affected candidates were at iON Digital Zone iDZ Sitapura centres, Jaipur, where the examination could not be completed due to an internal power supply problem. Despite repeated efforts, the issue could not be resolved, forcing National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS) to postpone the examination for the affected candidates.The health ministry has constituted a three-member committee to probe the power failure at the Jaipur centres. The panel comprises a senior Rajasthan govt official, a joint secretary-level officer from the health ministry and a chief engineer from the Central Electricity Authority.Dr Abhijat Sheth, president of NBEMS said re-examination for the 2,445 candidates will be conducted on Sept 5 at 3pm in Jaipur, with the board assuring that it will be conducted in the same manner and that the candidates' performance would not be adversely affected. "We regret the inconvenience caused to the affected candidates," he said.The nationwide examination was backed by extensive security and real-time monitoring. Around 2,527 faculty members were appointed as independent appraisers, while more than 700 senior faculty members, including deans, directors, medical superintendents and senior professors were deployed as flying squad members.Sixteen NBEMS regional command centres were operational across the country, while examination centres remained under live CCTV surveillance, monitored from the NBEMS headquarters in Dwarka.A dedicated team of 190 NBEMS and TCS personnel monitored the examination in real time. Officials from NBEMS, the health ministry, BEL, ECIL and TCS maintained continuous oversight from the central command centre. Aadhaar-based authentication of candidates was undertaken at examination centres as part of measures to strengthen security and prevent impersonation.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: A Norwegian farmer went to inspect an old mound in 1903 and uncovered a Viking ship buried with two women and hundreds of ancient objects
articles.summary: Rest of World News: On a farm near Tønsberg, Norway, a routine look inside an old burial mound in 1903 uncovered something that had been hidden for centuries. Farmer Oska.
articles.body: On a farm near Tønsberg, Norway, a routine look inside an old burial mound in 1903 uncovered something that had been hidden for centuries. Farmer Oskar Rom had been examining the mound on his property at Lille Oseberg when he came across what appeared to be pieces of an ancient ship. On August 8, he travelled to the capital to tell archaeologist Gabriel Gustafson what he had found. Gustafson quickly recognised that the remains could be far more significant than an ordinary burial.Within days, he was investigating the site himself. What lay beneath the mound would eventually include a Viking ship, the remains of two women and hundreds of objects, giving archaeologists an unusually detailed glimpse into life, craftsmanship and burial practices during the Viking Age.A farmer’s discovery leads archaeologists to a Viking ship graveOn August 8, 1903, Rom arrived in the capital with news from his property at Lille Oseberg in Slagen, Vestfold. He had been examining a large mound and had come across remains that suggested a ship was buried inside it.Gustafson, who oversaw the University’s Collection of National Antiquities, did not wait long before visiting the site. Within days, he had begun examining the mound. Decorated fragments emerging from the earth soon made the significance clearer: this was not an ordinary burial, but a Viking Age ship grave.The excavation itself had to wait until the following year, partly because of the approaching autumn weather. By then, the discovery had attracted public attention. Fences, signs and a guard were needed around the site, turning the excavation into something of a public spectacle.Gustafson was not entirely pleased with the attention. His diary records the difficulty of carrying out archaeological work while people gathered to watch.Inside the burial were hundreds of objects from Viking lifeThe ship had been badly crushed by the weight of the material covering it, but the burial had protected an extraordinary range of objects. As the excavation progressed, the team recovered a wagon, several sleds, carved animal heads, kitchen equipment, food remains, beds, tents and textiles.There were also remains of animals associated with the burial, including two cows, six dogs and fifteen horses. In total, several hundred objects were recovered.Many of these materials would normally have disappeared over the centuries. Wood, fabric and other organic objects rarely survive in such detail. Their presence at Oseberg meant archaeologists could study parts of Viking material culture that are usually missing from the archaeological record.The objects were not simply valuable possessions placed together at random. Their arrangement and variety offered clues about how people travelled, worked, dressed and prepared for death.Two women were buried inside the shipHuman remains were discovered in the burial chamber, belonging to two women. Their identities remain uncertain, but the scale and contents of the grave indicate that they occupied an important place within the society that buried them.The burial also appears to have been disturbed at some point not long after it took place. Someone had gained access to the grave, adding another layer to the history of the site.The presence of two women and the extraordinary quantity of goods in the chamber have made the burial particularly important for understanding women and status during the Viking Age. The grave provides evidence that reaches beyond the usual picture of Viking history centred on warfare and seafaring.The ship nearly became private propertyFinding the ship was only the beginning of the problem. In 1904, Norwegian cultural heritage law did not yet guarantee that an archaeological discovery belonged to the state. The owner of the land could therefore sell the find.The University had already spent 5,000 kroner on the excavation, leaving Gustafson and his colleagues facing the possibility that the ship could pass into private hands, or even leave Norway.That outcome was avoided when landowner Fritz Michael Treschow bought the entire discovery for 12,000 kroner and donated it to the University’s Collection of National Antiquities. Other benefactors then helped finance its preservation. Brewery owner Ellef Ringnes and consul Axel Heiberg contributed 6,000 kroner in 1905, while the city of Kristiania provided another 10,000 kroner.Without that support, the future of the ship and its contents could have been very different.Rebuilding the Oseberg ship took decadesThe excavation itself lasted three months. Preserving what had been uncovered was a far longer undertaking.The wooden remains had to be dried extremely slowly before the ship could be reconstructed. Conservators worked to preserve and reuse the original timbers wherever possible. The process of conservation and reconstruction eventually took 21 years.The result is remarkable for the amount of original material that survived. More than 90% of the wood in the reconstructed ship is original.The ship was never simply a vessel to be placed on display. Its survival allowed archaeologists to examine Viking shipbuilding techniques alongside the objects buried with it, creating a much broader picture of the people who built, used and ultimately buried it.What the Oseberg find revealed about Viking lifeThe significance of Oseberg lies partly in the things that survived alongside the ship. Textiles provide evidence of clothing and skilled textile work. Carved objects reveal artistic traditions and symbolism. Wooden furniture and equipment offer glimpses of domestic life that are rarely preserved elsewhere.The ship itself has also helped researchers understand Viking seafaring and construction. Together, the vessel and its contents provide evidence for a society capable of producing highly skilled woodwork, elaborate decoration and sophisticated textiles.The burial also offers a window into Viking attitudes towards death. The decision to place a ship and such a large collection of objects in a grave shows how material possessions, status, ritual and identity could become intertwined in burial practices.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Seven injured in violent clash in northern Germany
articles.summary: At least seven people were injured during a clash in northern Germany on Sunday. The incident took place in Hessisch Oldendorf, south-west of Hannover.
articles.body:
At least seven people were injured during a clash in northern Germany on Sunday.

The incident took place in Hessisch Oldendorf, south-west of Hannover.

Witnesses said the victims suffered stab and gunshot wounds, while several people were also run over by cars, the police reported.

The perpetrators fled the scene, but officers were able to detain two suspects later in the day and take them into police custody.

The police believe the alleged perpetrators have a connection to the victims. The circumstances are still under investigation.

Police were on the scene with a large number of officers, while there was also an increased police presence around the hospital in Hameln. The injured were taken to nearby hospitals.
